subject.title: fix(github-copilot): reject unsupported OAuth enterprise domain before refresh and model routing

question: Should legacy GitHub Copilot OAuth credentials be trusted only when their origin is github.com or a single-label *.ghe.com tenant root, with every other persisted origin withheld from model routing and forced through reauthentication?
rationale: This is the security-safe direction supported by the available provider documentation, but it also intentionally disables previously accepted persisted credentials and defines a permanent provider trust boundary that automation should not select without owner confirmation.

options.title: Confirm fail-closed allowlist
options.body: Accept only github.com and single-label *.ghe.com tenant roots, withhold unsupported legacy profiles, and require reauthentication.

options.title: Expand the supported contract
options.body: Identify any additional officially supported Copilot credential origins and cover their refresh, routing, and recovery behavior before merge.

options.title: Retire the legacy path
options.body: Pause this PR while replacing legacy core OAuth profiles with an explicit doctor migration into the plugin-owned credential path.

recommendation.title: Confirm fail-closed allowlist
recommendation.body: Accept only github.com and single-label *.ghe.com tenant roots, withhold unsupported legacy profiles, and require reauthentication.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent GitHub Copilot provider and plugin-boundary decisions make this person the strongest available routing candidate for the permanent trust and ownership contract.
